title: New European Fees Hit Shein's Cheap Fashion

source.author: FashionUnited
source.title: Shein warns of slow European recovery as EU import fees cut sales
source.note: Single source; FashionUnited attributes the figures to Reuters and marks the article as written with the assistance of AI. Percentage changes whose comparison period the source does not state (Europe -27.6%, US -9.4%, group -6%, marketing -41.5%, rest of world +18%) are left out; only the direction and the dollar amounts are used. The 17% rise in operating income is stated as year-on-year. 'Operating income' rendered as 'operating profit'; 'critical' as 'crucial'; 'cautious' as 'careful'.

paragraphs: Shein is an online fashion company that sells very cheap clothes to buyers around the world. Now it has warned that its business in Europe will stay under pressure until the second half of 2027. The reason is a set of new fees that the European Union has imposed on online orders that overseas sellers export to Europe. The news comes from Reuters, a news agency.

The European Union now imposes a fee of three euros on these exports. Shein's first tactic was to raise its prices to cover the extra cost. In the third quarter, the company's sales in Europe decreased to 2.98 billion dollars. Sales also decreased in the United States. As a result, sales for the whole group fell to 10.27 billion dollars.

The burden became heavier this month. At the start of November, the European Union added another fee of two euros. So the shopping season at the end of the year is uncertain for Shein. The fees are charged on each type of item in an order. A buyer who orders an outfit of five different items could pay 25 euros in fees. The company built its business on dresses for five euros and shoes for ten euros. With the fees, a cheap outfit is no longer so cheap.

"We expect the EU to remain under pressure for the next few quarters," said Sky Xu, the head of the company. Xu was speaking on a call with experts who study the company. According to Xu, sales in Europe might not recover until most orders are delivered from storage buildings inside Europe. Shein is investing in these buildings.

Shein's swift growth pushed rivals such as H&M and Zara to compete harder on price. Nevertheless, that swift growth has stopped. An old rule permitted small online orders from overseas to enter without tax. The United States and Europe have both canceled that rule. Now that it is canceled, nothing permits these orders to enter free. Cheap goods from overseas meet a new barrier.

Shein's second tactic was to cut its spending on marketing in the quarter. Most of the cut was in online advertising. The company sacrificed marketing to protect its profit. So profit went up while sales went down. Operating profit rose 17 percent compared with a year earlier, to 743 million dollars. In other words, Shein sacrificed growth and kept costs low.

Xu said that Shein is growing quickly in other regions, especially Latin America. Because of this, the company relies less on Europe and the United States. Sales in the rest of the world rose to 4.2 billion dollars. Xu also said that people around the world are becoming more careful with their money. For that reason, Xu added, it is still crucial to offer good value for money. This is crucial for Shein, because its business relies heavily on low prices.
